status: All fifteen Section II supplements approved by the current Run instruction; revalidation against effective entering law remains part of assembly.

matters.matter: Mid-Con Freight Systems, Inc. v. Michigan Public Service Commission
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm rejection of the §14504 preemption challenge to the separate §478.2(2) fee.

matters.matter: Eulitt v. Maine Department of Education
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm judgment against the parents' requested integrated-tuition funding claim and reject their unsupported assertion of the school's separate rights.

matters.matter: Kelo v. City of New London
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm the Connecticut judgment against the federal public-use challenge.
Affirm denial of the Rule 60 motion on the absence of extraordinary circumstances, while rejecting its classification as a successive habeas application.

matters.matter: Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Allapattah Services, Inc.
matters.controlled_disposition: In No. 04-70, affirm the Eleventh Circuit's supplemental-jurisdiction ruling. In consolidated No. 04-79, reverse the First Circuit insofar as it excludes the relatives' related claims solely for their individual amount deficiencies, and remand.
Affirm dismissal of the surviving direct action for want of an applicable §390uu waiver, without adopting an unnecessary beneficiary-merits determination.
Vacate the uncounseled first-tier disposition and remand for constitutionally adequate appellate consideration with appointed counsel.
Reverse the Ninth Circuit's relation-back ruling and remand for proceedings consistent with the common-core requirement.

matters.matter: Green Party of New York State v. New York State Board of Elections
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm the preliminary protection against the challenged enrollment exclusion and remand for continued proceedings under the stated functional scope.
Reverse the judgment sustaining the display and remand for effective prospective relief ending Texas's prohibited official presentation.

matters.matter: Town of Castle Rock v. Gonzales
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm the reinstatement of the procedural due-process claim against the Town, with the stated limits, and remand for adjudication of the remaining elements.
Reverse the amended Sixth Circuit judgment and remand for issuance of a mandate consistent with the earlier habeas disposition, subject to any independent lawful order not invalidated here.

matters.matter: McCreary County v. American Civil Liberties Union of Kentucky
matters.controlled_disposition: Affirm preliminary relief against the challenged current displays under the unified governmental-function inquiry and remand for continued proceedings.

matters.matter: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studios Inc. v. Grokster, Ltd.
matters.controlled_disposition: Vacate the defendants' summary judgment and remand for adjudication under the stated inducement rule and preserved independent theories.

matters.matter: National Cable & Telecommunications Association v. Brand X Internet Services
matters.controlled_disposition: In both No. 04-277 and consolidated No. 04-281, affirm the Ninth Circuit's judgment setting aside the FCC's exclusion of the described transmission offering from telecommunications-service treatment, on the statutory and judicial-precedent grounds stated here, and remand for lawful agency implementation.
